tagline: A wooded river gorge beside Walhalla’s fur-trade country
intro: West of Walhalla, the Pembina Gorge extends from the Canadian border through woodlands covering approximately 12,500 acres. Water cut the gorge into soft marine shale. It is one of the state’s deepest and steepest river valleys, where boreal forest, eastern deciduous forest and central grassland meet.

Walhalla’s history is tied to the Red River Valley fur trade. Norman Kittson established a trading post here in 1843 as an American Fur Company agent. The town followed in 1845, initially called St. Joseph after its Catholic mission. The Great Northern Railway reached Walhalla in 1898.
The western landmarks include Pembina Gorge State Park, six miles west of Walhalla. Walhalla itself stands beside the Pembina River, five miles from Manitoba. At Cavalier, the river is the Tongue.

moments.title: Pembina Gorge State Park
moments.text: Pembina Gorge State Park occupies a stretch of the Pembina River six miles west of Walhalla. Its recreation-area opening came in 2012; funding for conversion to North Dakota’s 14th state park followed in 2023. Construction began in May 2024, and the park opened to the public in June 2026. The surrounding gorge brings together boreal forest, eastern deciduous forest and central grassland. The gorge contains 30 plant species and 21 animal species categorized as rare in the state. Eight of the gorge’s plant species occur nowhere else in North Dakota. Over 480 species of vascular plants may be found here.

moments.title: Frost Fire Park
moments.text: At Frost Fire Park, the parking lot and lodge sit near the top of the ski runs. The ski area began in 1976, seven miles west of Walhalla. After 40 years, the Pembina Gorge Foundation bought the ski and snowboard area and renamed it Frost Fire Park as it expanded beyond a single season. In summer, eight downhill mountain-bike trails of varying difficulty use a chairlift to bring riders back to the top. The outdoor amphitheater adds another summer use, hosting plays and musicals alongside the park’s skiing and biking facilities.

moments.title: Walhalla
moments.text: The Kittson Trading Post, established in 1843 by American Fur Company agent Norman Kittson, is preserved in Walhalla State Historical Park. A different enterprise, the North West Company post established by David Thompson in 1797, moved in 1801 to a site one mile east of town. The building at that site is a reconstruction. Walhalla was originally named St. Joseph for the local Catholic mission. Nearby, the Gingras Trading Post State Historic Site preserves original buildings associated with trader and legislator Antoine Blanc Gingras, alongside a reproduction store and exhibits on Metis culture.
